title: A delegation request skipped every item change, so its uncertain delivery opened no delivery-acknowledgement item although section 8.1 asks one for each uncertain delivery
resolution: Only a delegation request's own item is skipped; the acknowledgement opens for any kind. Tests of a reported and a generation-end uncertain delegation result fail before the fix, and a mutant without acknowledgements fails the reported-delivery test.

title: An inbox answer to an item that a standing rule had closed failed with conflict already-answered instead of precondition-failed item-closed
resolution: The service's answerItem reads the item in the consuming transaction after the key check and refuses a resolved item with already-answered and a closed one with item-closed; an in-memory test and a PostgreSQL barrier race of a standing rule against an inbox answer fail before the fix.

title: The inbox answer's key was checked in the request's response scope, so a response key reused by an inbox answer repeated the response or reported a reused key instead of already-answered
resolution: An inbox answer's key is held in the item's scope, item and its ID, while the consumption of the request stays shared; in-memory and PostgreSQL tests that use one key in both channels, in both orders, fail before the fix.

title: listAgentSessions listed a card's sessions and read them in two transactions, so a page could show a session's newer state while missing a session added between them
resolution: The service's readCardSessions lists and reads the page in one transaction through the new SessionTimelineTransaction.scopes; a PostgreSQL barrier test that adds a session and submits a turn after the listing fails under a mutant that lists in a transaction of its own.

title: The in-memory scopes took a card only from existing sessions, so a root run without sessions was unknown in memory but a card on PostgreSQL, and no shared suite covered the port
resolution: The in-memory store reads an InMemoryTaskLineage of runs and tasks by the PostgreSQL rules, and SESSION_SCOPES_CONFORMANCE, with an empty card and a delegated child run, runs on both adapters; its card case fails under a mutant that derives cards from sessions.

title: The acknowledgement race test held its barrier at the read before the writing transactions, so they could run one after the other and the test proved no overlap
resolution: The barrier now waits after the item and key reads of each first writing attempt, and the test asserts three key reads, the loser's retry after the overlap; it fails under a mutant without the in-transaction state check, and every barrier wait is bounded with an assertion message.

title: The new acknowledgement path had no crash test of its item, audit event, and key committing together, and the request recording crash tests did not check the new item
resolution: Process crash tests kill an acknowledgement at SessionTimelineCommit.before and after and check the item, audit event, and key with the retry; the recording crash tests check the item. They fail under mutants that write no items or audit apart from the transaction.

title: The HTTP route tests shared the mutable session s-alpha, so the read test's counts held only when it ran before the tests that submit turns and answer requests
resolution: The read, submit, and respond tests each create a session of their own and s-alpha is reached only by refused commands; the old file with the read test moved last fails and the new one passes.

title: Both deltas put every item settlement in the transaction that changes the request, while an acknowledgement changes no request, and the unchanged-requests scenario forbade its item write
resolution: The session-turn-model and postgres-state requirements name the acknowledgement's own transaction with its audit event and key, the unchanged-requests scenario is limited to timeline changes, and scenarios cover the new behaviors.

title: The wrong-size key test was named as if it checked the digest's refusal, but it checked only that the file stayed and read back nine bytes
resolution: The test is named after what it checks; the refusal of the start stays covered by 13a's session-timeline-start test.

title: Task 3.1 stayed unticked although the record showed the merge, the route, a passing make verify, and the record written
The records presented passes 1 and 2 as always required, while policy version 8 stops the review after the first pass with only Low findings or none
resolution: Task 4.1 and the remaining gates state the passes conditionally under policy version 8.

title: A service comment still gave the held output tail to 13b after the split gave it to 13d
